title: Design a multi-tenant RAG system with data isolation
source: Popular question on AgentSwarms' GenAI interview list (asked at Stripe, Intercom, Shopify) and the GitHub AI system design list (alexeygrigorev); rubric is original
prompt: Design a RAG product that many companies use at once. Each company's documents must be searchable only by its own users, and no answer may mix data across companies.
functional: Each tenant uploads documents that only its users can search
Answers cite the tenant's own documents
Tenants can delete their data, including their vectors
non_functional: A query from one tenant never returns another tenant's chunk
Answers start within 2 seconds
One large tenant does not slow down the others
scale: 2,000 tenants, with the largest holding 50 million chunks
Peak of 500 queries per second across tenants
Documents change daily

components.name: Tenant-scoped vector storage
components.why: keeps each tenant's vectors separate so search cannot cross tenants

components.name: Access check on every query
components.why: the tenant filter is enforced on the server, not trusted from the client

components.name: Ingestion and embedding pipeline
components.why: turns uploaded documents into tenant-scoped chunks

components.name: LLM answer generation
components.why: writes the answer from the retrieved chunks with citations

components.name: Deletion and audit log
components.why: supports deletion requests and proves isolation

pitfalls: One shared index with the tenant filter applied in the client
Caching answers without the tenant in the cache key
Ignoring the noisy-neighbour problem for the largest tenant
Deleting documents but not their embeddings

title: Design a content moderation pipeline for user posts
source: Popular question on the GitHub AI system design list (content and policy violation detection); rubric is original
prompt: Design a system that checks every new user post for policy violations (hate, violence, spam, personal data) before or just after it goes live, and sends uncertain cases to human reviewers.
functional: Check text and images for policy violations
Hide or hold posts that violate policy
Send uncertain posts to a human review queue
non_functional: Most posts are checked within 2 seconds
Clear violations are blocked before they are visible
Reviewers' decisions improve the classifier over time
scale: 50 million posts per day, peak 3 times the average
About 2% of posts go to human review
Appeals are reviewed within 24 hours

components.name: Fast classifier layer
components.why: checks every post cheaply in real time

components.name: Escalation to a stronger model
components.why: handles borderline cases the fast layer cannot decide

components.name: Human review queue
components.why: keeps people in the loop for uncertain and disputed posts

components.name: Decision and feedback store
components.why: records decisions and feeds them back to improve the model

pitfalls: Waiting for a slow LLM on every post, which delays all posts
No way to appeal a removed post
Reviewers' labels never fed back into training
No audit trail of why a post was removed

title: Design a real-time fraud detection system for payments
source: Popular question on the GitHub AI system design list (alexeygrigorev/ai-engineering-field-guide) and AgentSwarms' interview list; rubric is original
prompt: Design a system that scores each card payment for fraud before it is approved. Legitimate payments must rarely be blocked, and new fraud patterns must be caught quickly.
functional: Score each payment before approval
Approve, challenge with a one-time code, or decline
Learn from confirmed fraud cases and chargebacks
non_functional: Decision within 100 ms, end to end
Less than 0.1% of good payments blocked
The system keeps working if the model service is slow (fallback rules)
scale: 10,000 payments per second at peak
Features for each card from the last 90 days
Models retrained each day

components.name: Real-time feature store
components.why: gives the model recent behaviour for this card and merchant within milliseconds

components.name: Scoring model service
components.why: gives each payment a fraud score

components.name: Rules and fallback
components.why: blocks known patterns and keeps decisions flowing if the model is slow

components.name: Event stream and training pipeline
components.why: feeds outcomes back so the model learns each day

components.name: Decision and case store
components.why: keeps every decision for disputes and audits

pitfalls: Calling a batch feature job during each payment, which misses recent activity
No fallback when the model times out, so payments fail
Training on labels without accounting for chargebacks that arrive weeks later
Measuring accuracy only, without the false-block rate on good payments

title: Design a customer support agent with human approval
source: Popular question on the AgentSwarms list (human-in-the-loop support agents, asked at Intercom and Klarna); rubric is original
prompt: Design an AI support agent that answers customers and can take actions such as refunds and address changes. Actions above a set amount or risk need a human to approve them.
functional: Answer customer questions using the help center and order data
Call tools: look up orders, issue refunds, change addresses
Pause for a human to approve risky actions, then continue
non_functional: A customer's first reply starts within 3 seconds
No refund is paid without the required approval
Every action is logged with who or what approved it
scale: 200,000 conversations per month
Average conversation has 6 turns and 3 tool calls
Peak of 500 human approvals per hour

components.name: Agent orchestrator
components.why: runs the model, calls tools, and tracks the conversation state

components.name: Tool layer with permissions
components.why: limits what the agent can do and checks each action against policy

components.name: Human approval queue
components.why: pauses risky actions until a person approves

components.name: Conversation and action log
components.why: keeps a record for disputes and for resuming after a pause

pitfalls: Letting the model call refund tools without a policy check
Approval waits with no timeout or handoff to a person
Losing the conversation state when the approval takes an hour
No way to stop the agent once it starts a loop of tool calls

title: Design a multi-step agentic workflow for scheduling and code review
source: Popular question on the GitHub AI system design list (multi-step agentic workflow such as meeting scheduling, code review, email campaigns); rubric is original
prompt: Design an agent system that completes multi-step jobs, such as scheduling a meeting across several calendars or reviewing a code change and filing comments. Each job may take minutes and call many tools.
functional: Break a goal into steps and run each step with tools
Resume a job after a crash or a tool failure
Stop safely when the job is off track or over budget
non_functional: A job never runs past its time and cost budget
No step runs twice after a retry
Users can see the progress of each job
scale: 50,000 jobs per day
Average job runs 12 steps and 40 model calls
Peak of 2,000 jobs running at once

components.name: Planner and step executor
components.why: turns the goal into steps and runs them in order

components.name: Durable job state
components.why: saves progress so a crash resumes instead of restarting

components.name: Tool gateway
components.why: one place to call calendars, repos, and email safely

components.name: Budget and loop guard
components.why: stops runaway jobs

components.name: Observability and traces
components.why: shows what each step did and why

pitfalls: No checkpoints, so a crash restarts the whole job and repeats emails
No cost or step limit, so a loop burns budget
Tools called directly from the model with no permission layer
Only the final answer logged, not the steps

title: Design an evaluation platform for 50 agent workflows
source: Popular question on the AgentSwarms list (eval platform, asked at Capital One, Stripe, Anthropic); rubric is original
prompt: Design a platform where a company's 50 AI agent workflows are tested before each release. It should catch regressions, compare model versions, and show results to product owners.
functional: Store test datasets for each workflow
Run evaluations on each new prompt, model, or code change
Compare results between versions and block a release on regression
non_functional: A full run finishes within 1 hour
Evaluations are reproducible
Test data containing customer information is kept inside the company
scale: 50 workflows with about 2,000 test cases each
Up to 200 evaluation runs per day
Each test case calls the model about 5 times with LLM-judged scoring

components.name: Dataset and test case store
components.why: keeps versioned test data so runs can be repeated

components.name: Parallel evaluation runners
components.why: run 100,000 model calls within an hour

components.name: Scorers including LLM judges
components.why: measures quality, including subjective answers

components.name: Results comparison and release gate
components.why: blocks a release on a regression and shows the difference

pitfalls: Judging with the same model version being tested, which biases the score
Non-reproducible runs because test data or model versions are not pinned
Running all 100,000 model calls sequentially
Test data with customer information sent to an outside judge model

title: Design a voice assistant for a hospital or call center
source: Popular question on the GitHub AI system design list (hospital voice assistant); rubric is original
prompt: Design a voice assistant that talks to callers in real time, answers common questions, books appointments, and hands off to a human when needed. Speech is noisy, and conversations contain private health or personal data.
functional: Listen to a caller and reply aloud in real time
Book, change or cancel an appointment through a system
Hand off to a human with a summary of the call
non_functional: Time from the caller stopping speaking to the reply starting is under 1 second
Personal data is encrypted and not used to train outside models
The assistant stays up during peak calls
scale: 10,000 concurrent calls at peak
Average call is 4 minutes
Medical vocabulary across 50 specialties

components.name: Streaming speech-to-text
components.why: turns speech into text while the caller is still talking

components.name: Language model with tools
components.why: decides the reply and calls the booking system

components.name: Streaming text-to-speech
components.why: speaks the reply without waiting for the full answer

components.name: Human handoff and call summary
components.why: passes hard calls to a person with context

components.name: Privacy controls
components.why: protects health data and removes it from logs

pitfalls: Waiting for the caller to finish and then transcribing the whole call, which adds seconds of silence
Logging full transcripts with personal and health data
No handoff when the caller asks for a person
Ignoring noise and medical vocabulary in the speech model

title: Design cross-conversation memory for a chat assistant
source: Popular question on the IGotAnOffer and GitHub AI system design lists (ChatGPT cross-conversation memory); rubric is original
prompt: Design the memory feature of a chat assistant. It should remember useful facts about a user across conversations, let the user see and delete them, and keep prompts within the model's context limit.
functional: Save facts the user shares or confirms
Recall relevant memories when a new conversation starts
Let users view, edit, and delete memories
non_functional: Memory recall adds under 150 ms
Deleted memories are removed from all stores within 24 hours
A wrong memory can be corrected by the user
scale: 100 million users, about 30 memories each on average
Peak of 20,000 new chats per second
Each prompt has room for about 2,000 tokens of memory

components.name: Memory extraction
components.why: decides which facts are worth remembering

components.name: Memory store with per-user access
components.why: keeps each user's memories private and deletable

components.name: Retrieval and ranking
components.why: picks the few memories that matter for the current chat

components.name: Prompt budget
components.why: fits memories into the context window without crowding out the conversation

pitfalls: Injecting all memories into every prompt, which exceeds the context limit
Deleting memories from the UI but not from backups or indexes
Saving sensitive data such as passwords or health information without consent
No way for a user to correct a wrong memory

title: Design an AI answer engine with live web search and citations
source: Popular question on the GitHub AI system design list (Perplexity-style real-time LLM search); rubric is original
prompt: Design a search product that answers a question in a few paragraphs, using fresh web results, and cites each claim with its source. It should answer follow-up questions quickly.
functional: Search the web for a question and read the top results
Write an answer where each claim links to a source
Answer follow-up questions in the same session quickly
non_functional: First words of the answer appear within 2 seconds
Sources are never invented; claims without a source are removed
Results are no more than 1 hour old for news queries
scale: 200 million queries per day
Each query reads about 10 pages
Peak of 10,000 queries per second

components.name: Query understanding and search
components.why: finds fresh and relevant pages for the question

components.name: Page fetch and extraction cache
components.why: avoids fetching and parsing the same page repeatedly

components.name: Answer generation with citations
components.why: writes the answer from the sources with links

components.name: Citation check
components.why: removes claims the sources do not support

components.name: Streaming response
components.why: shows the answer as it is written

pitfalls: Generating the answer before the search results are fetched
Citing a source that does not contain the claim
No freshness rule, so old news is answered as current
Fetching the same popular pages for every query with no cache
